title: The Run Out (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational cricket philosophy 104bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal absurdist sport
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The run out is the worst way to end a batting innings by a mile
You haven't been bowled or caught — you've been done by a lack of style
A direct hit on the stumps from twenty-two yards at pace
And the replays show you were halfway between two places

[Pre-Chorus]
There's always a hesitation — a conversation in the middle
One batsman going, one not going, the universe a riddle

[Chorus]
The run out is a tragedy in real time and in slow
Two men, one ball, one call that turned out wrong to go
The run out is a lesson in the value of one voice
When two people have opinions it creates a difficult choice
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The fielder dives and gathers and releases in a throw
The stumps light up before the bat is in the crease below
The batsman stands and looks back at the place he should have been
The most honest sporting failure you'll ever have seen

[Bridge]
The call is yours, the call is mine, the call belongs to neither
The run out happens somewhere in between the two believers
Someone should have called it, someone should have sent them back
The run out is a miscommunication — that's the fact

[Outro]
Run out knows… two calls, no call, wrong call… run out knows
That's my boy
